item.title: Optimising multipartite entanglement manipulation in quantum networks
item.description:
📚 arXiv
👤 Shashank Shekhar, David Elkouss, Siddhartha Santra
arXiv:2610.21420v1 Announce Type: new Abstract: Long-range, genuine multipartite entanglement (GME) between distant parties in a quantum network is a crucial resource for distributed quantum information processing. Through controlled manipulation of short-range GME states in the network via stochastic local operations aided by classical communication (SLOCC), long-range GME can be established between selected target nodes on demand. Optimizing such multipartite entanglement distribution protocols under constraints imposed by the network architecture, target-node set, and available resource budget is a key challenge in resource-efficient manipulation of GME. We present a general operational framework for manipulating GME in quantum networks by classifying the relevant networking operations…

item.title: SynDebug: A Framework to Debug Logic Bugs in Fault-Tolerant Quantum Computing Programs
item.description:
📚 arXiv
👤 Nicholas S. DiBrita, Jack Lange, Tirthak Patel
arXiv:2610.22275v1 Announce Type: new Abstract: Fault-tolerant quantum computing (FTQC) introduces substantial systems-level complexity through quantum error correction (QEC), making debugging FTQC programs challenging. Existing quantum debugging approaches primarily target logical-level circuits and do not naturally support debugging within realistic FTQC execution flows. We present SynDebug, the first systems-level debugging framework for FTQC programs. SynDebug introduces lightweight assertion-based debugging primitives that operate directly within encoded FTQC infrastructures while avoiding additional logical surface area and minimizing temporal overhead. We evaluate SynDebug across multiple QEC code families, code distances, and encoded workloads, including state preparation, entangl…

item.title: Theory of two-qubit T₂ spectroscopy of quantum many-body systems
item.description:
📚 Phys. Rev. B
👤 Hossein Hosseinabadi, Pavel E. Dolgirev, Sarang Gopalakrishnan, Amir Yacoby, Eugene Demler, and Jamir Marino
Author(s): Hossein Hosseinabadi, Pavel E. Dolgirev, Sarang Gopalakrishnan, Amir Yacoby, Eugene Demler, and Jamir Marino Qubit sensing is rapidly emerging as a powerful way to probe quantum systems. Here, the authors demonstrate how measuring correlations between two qubits, both coupled to the same quantum many-body system, can uncover crucial information about the system itself. These correlations reveal how excitations and fluctuations propagate through space and time, distinguish ballistic from diffusive transport, and provide a sensitive probe of how far the system is driven from equilibrium. [Phys. Rev. B 114, 214416] Published Fri Oct 16, 2026

arXiv:2610.22205v1 Announce Type: cross Abstract: The paradigm of a simple unstable theory in the sense of Shelah is the theory of the random graph, the Fraïssé limit of the finite graphs. item.description:

👤 Saba Arife Bozpolat
本研究提出了一种广义的n比特超密编码协议，利用纠缠的n量子比特系统和n-1个量子比特的传输，实现n个经典比特的信息传输。该协议涉及创建最大纠缠的n量子比特GHZ态，使用Pauli-Z和Pauli-X门编码经典消息，并通过量子通信、量子操作和测量进行传输和解码。其核心创新在于一个显式、可扩展的n比特编码例程，仅使用单量子比特Pauli-X和Pauli-Z操作在GHZ信道上实现低深度编码层。该协议在IBM量子硬件上进行了概念验证，结果显示成功率随消息长度、转译电路深度和门计数增加而降低。
